skyline_extract — GEOCAM skyline op

• Data kinds: image2d → signal

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.skyline_extract(image, sky_is_bright=True, smooth=1.5, max_jump=3, jump_penalty=0.5) (to call the implementation directly, import geocam; geocam.skyline_extract(image, sky_is_bright=True, smooth=1.5, max_jump=3, jump_penalty=0.5); from the registry, opsgeocam.get("skyline_extract"))

Usage

Extracts from a photo, by dynamic programming, 1 line giving the row of the sky–terrain boundary for each column → signal (W,).

Same idea as Lie, Lin, and Hsu 2005 (*Pattern Recognition*: Robust Skyline Extraction for Navigation):

Changes in brightness in the vertical direction (if the sky is bright above, I[v−1] − I[v+1] is positive) are considered boundary-likeness'', Choose the path with the lowest cost among consecutive paths that do not jump more than max_jump rows from the next column (jump_penalty × line jump). Even if there is a locally strong response at the vertical edges of clouds or buildings, the path Continuity leaves real ridgelines.

Args:

image: (H, W) float. For RGB, make it gray first.

sky_is_bright: The sky is brighter than the terrain (daytime). False if it is reversed in night view/backlight.

smooth: Vertical Gaussian σ [pixels] (noise). 0 disables.

max_jump: Allowed row jump in adjacent columns [pixels].

jump_penalty: Cost per jump pixel (boundary likelihood is normalized from 0 to 1).

Returns:

signal (W,) float: Boundary row for each column (0 is the top row). Only the sky/topography is shown

In images that are not shown, the average boundary response is close to 0, so ValueError

Stop at (silence and do not return the noise line).
